Cc: Horizon Legal <legal@horizonretail.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: third-party IP responsibility

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal asked me to surface a couple of hot spots in the MSA and Order Form for our procurement review. The primary item is: Horizon needs clarity that a vendor indemnifies us for third-party IP claims that arise from the service (including alleged infringement tied to model outputs or supplied models).

We submitted redlines attached (Horizon_MSA_redlines_v2.docx) that: (1) require vendor to defend and indemnify Horizon for third-party IP infringement claims reasonably related to the service; (2) require vendor to procure any right to use models/datasets not owned by Horizon; and (3) limit indemnity to direct damages but carve out punitive/exemplary. We flagged the outputs question — we’re proposing a narrow obligation where vendor must remediate or replace any portion of the service if a third party asserts infringement tied to product outputs.

Can you confirm Redwood’s position so we can move the Order Form forward? Timing: procurement would like a legal confirmation before Aug 21.

Thanks,
Claire Zhou
Head of Strategic Sourcing
Horizon Retail

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: third-party IP responsibility

Claire —

Appreciate the clear redlines and timeline. Looping in Marissa (customer lead) and Rishi (legal) so we can coordinate an answer. High-level view from my side: Redwood is comfortable accepting indemnity for third-party claims that are caused by Redwood’s own IP (e.g., the model weights we deliver, our serving code) or by our willful misconduct. We are reluctant to accept broad indemnity for customer outputs — that creates open-ended exposure for downstream prompt-dependent results.

Proposed near-term compromise: we offer to indemnify and defend Horizon for third-party IP claims to the extent they arise from (a) Redwood-provided models or software that infringe third-party IP; or (b) Redwood’s breach of its representations in the MSA (including representations about having rights to models/datasets we supply). For alleged infringement based on customer-provided prompts or outputs, we propose a remediation/replace remedy + joint defense/notice procedure rather than automatic indemnity.

Rishi — can you propose redline language and a cap/limitation approach we can share? Marissa — I want to align on negotiation posture (discount/credits if we accept broader terms).

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa —

Drafted suggested language below for Redwood’s response. I recommend we present this as a balanced compromise that preserves our risk profile while addressing Horizon’s commercial need. Key points:

- Redwood Indemnity: Redwood will defend and indemnify Horizon for third-party claims alleging direct infringement to the extent such claims arise from (i) Redwood’s willful infringement; or (ii) use of Redwood-delivered model weights or software that incorporate infringing third-party material.
- Customer Outputs / Model Results: For claims alleging infringement arising solely from customer prompts or generated outputs, Redwood will not provide an open-ended indemnity. Instead, Redwood will (A) promptly investigate upon notice; (B) use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate or replace the affected service/component; and (C) share reasonable costs for remediation where the claim is demonstrably traceable to Redwood-delivered artifacts.
- Defense Control & Participation: Redwood will have primary control of the defense but Horizon may participate with counsel of its choosing at its own expense; Redwood will not settle any claim that imposes liability on Horizon without Horizon’s prior consent.
- Caps & Remedies: Indemnity limited to direct damages; cap equals the fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, subject to exceptions for willful misconduct.

Action items: I will convert to tracked redlines (Redwood_proposed_redlines_v1.docx) and Marissa — please confirm whether you want us to offer a limited escrow/holdback mechanism as a commercial sweetener.

Rishi Malhotra
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Claire —

Thanks again — attached is Redwood’s proposed compromise and the playbook that explains how we triage IP claims (Redwood_Response_IP_Playbook.pdf). Highlights of the proposed MSA redline (attached Redwood_proposed_redlines_v1.docx):

1) Redwood will indemnify Horizon for third-party IP infringement claims to the extent such claims are directly caused by Redwood’s models or software (including willful infringement).
2) For alleged infringement tied to customer-generated outputs, Redwood proposes remediation/replace + participation in defense rather than open-ended indemnity. We’ve included a short escalation path and SLA for investigation (48 hours acknowledgement, 10 business day initial findings).
3) Defense control language: Redwood retains primary control, Horizon may participate; Redwood will not settle to impose liability on Horizon without consent.
4) Cap: indemnity limited to direct damages up to the Order Form fees in the prior 12 months (exceptions for willful misconduct).

We’re open to a commercial bridge (small holdback or limited escrow) if Horizon needs stronger financial comfort while the parties finalize language.

Document links: https://docusign.example.com/xyz-orderform-4729 (order form draft)

Please let us know any specific language edits by EOD Monday Aug 17 and we’ll try to turn a final form the same day.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the playbook — that helped clarify your operational approach. Horizon can accept Redwood’s indemnity for vendor-supplied models/software as proposed. A few remaining asks before final sign: 

1) For outputs: instead of an exclusion we’d like an explicit commitment that Redwood will (a) promptly remediate or replace when an infringement claim is valid, and (b) reimburse direct, reasonable costs that Horizon incurs to the extent the claim is demonstrably linked to a Redwood-supplied artifact. That is narrower than full indemnity but gives us operational and financial protection.
2) We want the notice and investigation SLAs captured in the Order Form.
3) Please confirm Redwood will not assert limitations (e.g., waiver of warranty) that would defeat the indemnity.

Assuming those changes, procurement expects to sign the Order Form and proceed with a pilot. Our legal team will send a final mark if needed but timeline is to close by Aug 20.
